exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
instructions: Set up in a push-up position with the hands well outside shoulder width and the body in one line.
Lower toward one hand, bending that elbow while the other arm stays long out to the side.
Stop when the chest is just above the floor and the hips are still square.
Press back to the middle through the bent arm and repeat to the other side.
exercises.formCue: Load the bent arm, keep the hips level.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting or shifting the hips to cheat the load, and rushing the change of sides.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use regular push-ups until they are solid, then try archers with the hands on a bench.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It puts most of your weight on one arm, which is the bridge between two-arm and one-arm pressing.

exercises.name: One-Arm Push-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Chest, triceps, front delts, lats, obliques, glutes
instructions: Take a push-up position with the feet wider than the hips and one hand under the shoulder, the other off the floor.
Tighten everything from grip to glutes to quads before you move.
Lower under control with the shoulder packed down and the trunk turning as little as possible.
Press the floor away to a straight arm without letting the plank break.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag or rotate, shrugging the working shoulder, and the feet rolling inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the working hand on a bar or bench and lower the height over weeks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds heavy pressing strength and cross-body trunk control with no equipment.

exercises.name: Elevated One-Arm Push-Up
exercises.equipment: Bar in a rack, bench or sturdy box
instructions: Place one hand on a fixed bar or bench and walk the feet back into a wide-stance plank.
Put the free hand behind the back or along the thigh and tense the whole body.
Lower the chest toward the hand with the shoulders as level as you can keep them.
Press back to a straight arm, then finish all reps before switching sides.
exercises.formCue: Same tension as the floor version, just a kinder angle.
exercises.commonMistakes: Picking a height that is too low and twisting to finish the rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the hand at hip height and only lower it when every rep stays square.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you practise the exact one-arm pattern at a load you can own.

exercises.name: Planche Lean
exercises.musclesWorked: Front delts, serratus, biceps tendon area, wrists, core
instructions: Start in a straight-arm plank with the fingers forward or turned slightly out.
Lock the elbows with the elbow pits facing forward and press the shoulders down away from the ears.
Lean forward until the shoulders travel past the wrists and hold.
Rock back to the plank before the elbows bend or the hips drop.
exercises.formCue: Arms locked, lean from the ankles.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows as the lean gets hard, and skipping wrist preparation.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lean only a few centimetres and build time before adding distance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the straight-arm shoulder strength every planche step depends on.

exercises.name: Frog Stand
instructions: Squat down and plant the hands shoulder width apart with the elbows bent out to make a shelf.
Rest the knees on the arms just above the elbows.
Tip forward slowly until the toes get light, then let them leave the floor.
Look slightly ahead, breathe evenly and hold, then tip back onto the feet.
exercises.formCue: Tip forward slowly, eyes ahead of the hands.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping into the balance instead of leaning into it, and holding the breath.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the toes on the floor, or rest the forehead on a folded towel while you find the lean.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the wrists and shoulders to carry your full weight before harder hand balances.

exercises.name: Tuck Planche
exercises.musclesWorked: Front delts, serratus, chest, core, wrists
instructions: From a frog stand or a seated start on parallettes, lock the arms straight.
Lean the shoulders ahead of the hands and press the floor away to round the upper back.
Pull the knees to the chest and lift the feet and knees clear of the arms.
Hold with the hips near shoulder height, then set the feet down with control.
exercises.formCue: Lean, lock, push the floor away.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bent elbows, and rushing here before the wrists and shoulders are ready.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the frog stand, then take one knee off the arm at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the first real planche hold and a strong test of straight-arm pressing.

exercises.name: Ring Push-Up
instructions: Set the rings low and take a plank with a hand in each ring, arms straight.
Keep the body in one line from head to heels.
Lower the chest between the rings while keeping them close to the ribs.
Press to full lockout without letting the rings swing or drift apart.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rings drifting wide and hips sagging as the set goes on.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the rings so the body is more upright, or use regular push-ups.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The unstable handles make the shoulders and trunk work harder than the floor version.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Inverted Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Mid back, lats, rear delts, biceps
exercises.equipment: Fixed bar and bench or box
instructions: Lie under a fixed bar, take a wide overhand grip and rest the heels on a bench.
Hang with straight arms and a straight body.
Pull the chest to the bar and draw the shoulders back at the top.
Lower until the arms are straight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hips dropping and the chin reaching for the bar instead of the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put the feet on the floor, or bend the knees.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Raising the feet makes the row close to a full bodyweight horizontal pull.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, teres major, rear delts, biceps, forearms
instructions: Grip the bar overhand, hands clearly wider than the shoulders.
Hang with the arms and shoulders fully extended.
Pull until the chin is over the bar.
Lower all the way to a straight-arm hang.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going so wide that the range gets short, and stopping before a full hang.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a band, or do slow lowering reps with this grip.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It shifts more of the pull to the lats and upper back.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
instructions: Take the parallel handles with the palms facing each other.
Hang with the arms and shoulders fully extended.
Pull until the neck reaches the height of the hands.
Lower to a full hang under control.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, elbows to the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking the legs and stopping short at the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a band or a foot on a box to take some weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The palms-in grip is often the most comfortable way to pull heavy for elbows and shoulders.

exercises.name: L Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip.
Lift the straight legs until they are level with the hips and hold them there.
Pull the chin over the bar without letting the legs drop or swing.
Lower to a full hang with the legs still held in the L.
exercises.commonMistakes: Legs dropping as you pull, and using a swing to start the rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a tucked-knee position during the pull-up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Holding the L removes all momentum and trains the trunk while you pull.

exercises.name: Ring Support Hold
instructions: Grip the rings and press or jump to straight arms above them.
Lock the elbows and pull the shoulders down away from the ears.
Turn the rings out slightly so the palms face forward.
Hold the rings still against the sides, then step down before the arms bend.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bent elbows, shrugged shoulders and rings shaking away from the body.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the toes on a box to take some weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A steady support is the base for every dip and muscle-up on rings.

exercises.name: False Grip Hang
instructions: Set the rings so the heel of each hand sits on top of the ring, wrist bent over it.
Wrap the fingers and let the ring rest across the base of the palm.
Hang with the wrists still bent, feet on the floor at first if needed.
Come down before the grip slips back into the fingers.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the ring slide into the fingers, and holding too long too soon.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the feet on the floor in a ring-row position and hold the grip there.
exercises.whyThisMatters: This grip is what lets you move from the pull to the dip in a strict muscle-up.

exercises.name: Strict Ring Muscle-Up
instructions: Hang from the rings in a false grip.
Pull smoothly and as high as you can, bringing the rings to the chest.
Lean the chest forward over the hands and bring the elbows back to move above the rings.
Press out of the dip to locked arms with the rings turned slightly out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Losing the false grip, and trying it before strict pull-ups and dips are solid.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the transition with the feet on the floor under low rings.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It links a pull and a press into one skill that gets you on top of the rings.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hip flexors, ankles, core
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other leg held out in front and the arms forward for balance.
Sit back slightly and bend the standing knee, letting it track over the toes with the heel down.
Lower until the hip crease is below the knee.
Drive through the whole foot to stand without the free leg touching the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rocking onto the toes, the knee caving in, and the free foot touching down.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a box, hold a support, or let the free heel rest lightly on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds single-leg strength, balance and ankle range together.

exercises.name: Box Pistol Squat
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a box or bench with the other leg held forward.
Sit back and down under control until you touch the box.
Keep the standing knee in line with the foot.
Stand up on the same leg without rocking for momentum.
exercises.formCue: Touch the box, do not drop onto it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Falling the last few centimetres and bouncing back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a higher box and lower it over time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The box sets a depth you can control while single-leg strength catches up.

exercises.name: Assisted Pistol Squat
instructions: Hold a rack upright or other fixed support at chest height.
Stand on one leg with the other leg held in front.
Lower as deep as you can control, using the hands only as much as needed.
Stand up through the whole foot, keeping the pull from the arms light.
exercises.formCue: Legs do the work, hands just guide.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hauling yourself up with the arms and letting the heel lift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the depth and add range as control improves.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you practise the full pistol path before you have the strength to do it free.

exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
instructions: Stand on one leg and bend the other knee so that foot is behind you.
Reach the arms forward and keep the weight over the middle of the standing foot.
Lower slowly until the back knee touches the floor softly behind the standing heel.
Stand back up without pushing off the back foot.
exercises.formCue: Weight on the midfoot, knee kisses the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the back knee hard and pushing off the rear toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the knee to a pad or stack of mats to shorten the range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds one-leg strength and scales more easily than the pistol.

exercises.name: L-Sit
exercises.musclesWorked: Abs, hip flexors, quads, triceps, shoulders
instructions: Sit with the legs straight and the hands flat beside the hips, or grip parallettes.
Press down hard and push the shoulders away from the ears.
Lift the hips and both straight legs off the floor.
Hold with the knees locked and chest tall, then lower with control.
exercises.formCue: Push down, shoulders low, knees locked.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugged shoulders, a rounded back and bent knees.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a tuck with the knees bent, or keep one foot on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk and hip flexors hard while the arms support the body.

exercises.name: Tuck L-Sit
instructions: Sit between the hands or parallettes with the knees bent.
Press down and push the shoulders away from the ears until the hips lift.
Pull the knees toward the chest so both feet leave the floor.
Hold with a tall chest, then set the feet down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sinking into the shoulders and leaning back to lift the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift one foot at a time while the other stays down.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the support strength and compression needed for the full L-sit.

exercises.name: Tuck Front Lever
instructions: Hang from a bar or rings with straight arms.
Pull the knees tight to the chest and lean back, pressing the hands down toward the hips.
Raise the hips until the back is roughly level with the floor.
Hold with the arms locked, or lower slowly into the position from above, then return to the hang.
exercises.formCue: Straight arms, push the bar to the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows and letting the hips hang low.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do slow lowering reps from an inverted tuck before holding.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the first front lever step and builds straight-arm pulling strength.

exercises.name: Advanced Tuck Front Lever
instructions: Start in a tuck front lever with the arms straight.
Open the hips so the knees move away from the chest and the back flattens.
Keep the hips level with the shoulders.
Hold for a short time, then tuck back in and lower to the hang.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, hips at shoulder height.
exercises.commonMistakes: Opening the tuck further than you can hold, so the hips drop.
exercises.beginnerModification: Go back to the tight tuck or use slow lowering reps.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Moving the knees away lengthens the lever and loads the lats more.

exercises.name: Tuck Back Lever
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, chest, biceps, lower back, glutes
instructions: Hang from the rings, tuck the knees and roll backward between the arms until inverted.
Keep the knees tucked and the arms straight.
Lower the hips slowly behind you until the back is level with the floor, chest facing down.
Hold briefly, then pull back to the inverted tuck and roll out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping in fast, and forcing the range when the shoulders are not ready.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work on shoulder extension flexibility and lower only part of the way.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the shoulders in extension and the muscles along the back of the body.

exercises.name: Chest-to-Wall Handstand
instructions: Start in a plank with the feet against a wall.
Walk the feet up the wall and the hands in until you are near vertical, chest facing the wall.
Stack wrists, shoulders and hips, push tall through the shoulders and keep the body tight.
Hold while breathing steadily, then walk back down before you tire.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the back and walking in closer than you can safely exit from.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stop at a shallower angle with the hands further from the wall.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Facing the wall teaches a straight handstand line and builds time upside down.

exercises.name: Handstand Kick-Up
instructions: Stand facing a wall, place the hands shoulder width apart a short distance from it and lock the arms.
Step into a short lunge and swing the back leg up while the front leg pushes off lightly.
Let the lead heel touch the wall softly, with the legs still split.
Bring the legs together, hold, then step down one leg at a time.
exercises.formCue: Kick soft enough to barely touch.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking too hard and bending the arms on the way up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise small kicks that only reach halfway.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A controlled entry is what makes handstand practice repeatable and safe.

exercises.name: Freestanding Handstand
instructions: Kick up gently in clear space with the arms locked and hands shoulder width apart.
Pause with the legs split, then close them into one straight line.
Balance by pressing through the fingers when you tip over and through the heel of the hand when you fall back.
Step down, or turn out sideways like a cartwheel if you overbalance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking too hard, and practising before you have a safe way to bail.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work near a wall and float the heels off it for a second at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It develops shoulder strength, balance and body awareness in one skill.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from a high bar with an overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders.
Keep the knees straight and the body still.
Raise the legs by bending at the hips until they are at least level with the hips.
Lower them slowly to the hang without swinging.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging to throw the legs up and dropping them on the way down.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees and do hanging knee raises.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the abs and hip flexors through a long range while training grip.
